newsitem.title: USA: Texaco Marathon set deepwater effort.
newsitem.headline: Texaco Marathon set deepwater effort.

text.p: Texaco Inc and USX Corp's Marathon Oil Co said Tuesday they are moving ahead with construction of "Petronius," a $400 million deepwater Gulf of Mexico project designed to develope oil and natural gas reserves estimated at 80-100 million barrels of oil equivalent.
They said first production from Petronius is expected in January 1999. Production design capacity is 60,000 barrels of oil and 100 million cubic feet of natural gas daily.
The project is located on Viosca Knoll Block 786, 130 miles southeast of New Orleans.
Texaco, the Petronius project operator, said a $140 million contract for construction and installation of the compliant tower was awarded to J. Ray McDermott.
Part of a new generation of fixed platforms, a compliant tower is similar to a traditional platform, McDermott explained in a separate statement.

However, unlike their predecessors, compliant towers are designed to flex with the forces of waves, wind, and current. This unique design uses less steel than a conventional platform in an equal water depth, making it less costly.

The company said its marine operations will install the tower over two work seasons. Installation of the foundation in 1,754 feet of water will take place in 1997. The topsides and two tower sections will be installed in 1998.
Both installation procedures will utilize the company's dynamically positioned Derrick Barge 50, McDermott said.

Texaco also said Gulf Island Fabrication received a $50 million deck fabrication and integration contract, and W. H. Linder & Associates a contract valued at about $10 million for engineering design work of the topsides and procurement support.

In addition to these platform contracts, the costs for Petronius' drilling and production facilities, including compression, process and injection systems, and living quarters, coupled with drilling and construction of pipeline infrastructure, bring the total cost of the Petronius project to about $400 million, Texaco said.
Owned 50/50 by Texaco and Marathon, Petronius will be the first of three deepwater projects discovered in 1995 to begin production, Texaco said. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
